subject: humanities
passage: Editors at literary magazines often say that poetry is the hardest category in which to be published, because so many poems are submitted for so few pages. Editor Marguerite Dubois examined the submissions received by a quarterly magazine in Montreal, Canada, during 2023 to see whether this was true at her own magazine. She found that poetry was indeed the most competitive category, though not because it received the most submissions: ______

data.title: Submissions and Acceptances at a Montreal Literary Magazine, 2023

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?

choices.A: translations had the highest acceptance rate because the magazine struggled to find enough translators.
choices.B: short fiction received 2,840 submissions, more than any other category, and had the lowest acceptance rate.
choices.C: poetry had the lowest acceptance rate, 0.6 percent, even though short fiction received far more submissions.
choices.D: poetry received 1,960 submissions, the second-largest number of any category.

explanation.why: "Most competitive" means the smallest share of submissions accepted, so look at the acceptance rate column: poetry's 0.6 percent is the lowest. The statement adds that this was not because poetry had the most submissions, so the choice must also note that short fiction received more (2,840 versus 1,960).
explanation.A: Incorrect. Translations did have the highest rate, but the table offers no reason for it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Short fiction did receive the most submissions, but its acceptance rate (0.8 percent) was not the lowest; poetry's (0.6 percent) was.
explanation.C: Correct. Poetry's acceptance rate was the lowest of the four categories even though short fiction had far more submissions, which matches both parts of the statement.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is true, but the number of submissions alone does not show how competitive a category is, and the statement says submissions were not the reason.
